scenes.text: This is Odysseus. It is an autonomous SSI index-deviation agent built for on-chain fund operators. It acts as a self-contained fund manager that identifies mispriced deviations in SoSoValue indexes and executes relative-value trades on SoDEX. It is built for teams that value discipline, not prediction. The key is that it is built to say no trade by default.

Let's go to the console. I'll connect my operator wallet and click Run Pipeline. The agent immediately fetches data from the SoSoValue API, validates the klines, and calculates the z-scores for the MAG7 constituents. Every run stores the validated snapshot, the deviation signals, and the audit trail, so operators can inspect the decision.

Here is the core of Odysseus. Instead of just blindly trading, it runs an adversarial debate. The Bull Agent argues why the deviation is a mispricing. The Bear Agent argues why the move is justified, or why execution risk is too high. The Chief Agent reviews both, and makes the final verdict. The Chief is constrained: it can only choose SHORT or NO_TRADE.

Once the Chief approves a short, the deterministic Risk Engine runs five hard checks: spread, depth, and confidence. Because the SoDEX testnet currently lacks spot liquidity, the agent simulates the spot hedge, but it executes the real perps short on the SoDEX testnet. You can see the real order I D right here. If any gate fails, no order is sent.

Every run is saved. Operators can go to the Replay page to re-run historical snapshots instantly. Odysseus proves that a single person can run a risk-managed, on-chain fund with zero manual intervention. The live console and the complete source code are linked on screen. Every number shown here comes from a persisted run. Thank you.
